entries.title: South Korea's $1 Trillion Export Phenomenon | Armstrong Economics
entries.paragraph_1: South Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports, becoming only the fourth country in history to reach that milestone, joining the United States, Germany, and China. This is a country that emerged from the Korean War devastated, impoverished, and dependent upon foreign assistance. In the 1960s, Koreans were exporting wigs made from human hair, squid, pig bristles, and whatever else they could sell to earn foreign currency. Today, they are producing the semiconductors powering the global artificial intelligence revolution. entries.paragraph_2: Korean exports have increased more than 36,000-fold since 1948. As recently as 1964, annual exports were only $100 million. entries.paragraph_1: Yet within minutes, the warning evaporated only to be replaced by a cascade of contradictory messages that blamed North Korean planes for an incursion that never happened. South Korean authorities mistook a routine provocation for aÂ complete invasion by North Korea, blaming the wrong country exaggeratedly and entirely. The Russian flyby, the mistaken alerts, and the ensuing confusion reveal deeper rot of a system that conditions populations to fear phantom enemies. Key points: Several Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defense identification zone near Ulleung Island prompting a brief emergency alert. South Korean fighter jets scrambled but the aircraft did not violate sovereign airspace. The Interior Ministry issued an evacuation warning that was lifted three minutes later. North Gyeongsang Province mistakenly described the aircraft as suspected North Korean planes using an outdated drill template. South Korea plans to summon a Russian diplomat to lodge a formal protest. The incident follows multiple recent Russian entries into the zone amid heightened Korean Peninsula tensions. AIR RAID evacuation warning turns out to be false alarm When the Interior Ministry's text message hit phones at 7:52 a.m. commanding "EVACUATION, AIR RAID," residents of Ulleung Island had every reason to believe the worst. This is a community still haunted by November 2022 when a North Korean missile screaming toward their island triggered real sirens and civilians scattered with no clue where to seek refuge. But this time the threat was not a missile but a flight of Russian aircraft that never violated South Korean airspace, only its monitoring zone. An air defense identification zone is not sovereign territory but a buffer where a country tracks approaching planes. Russian military aircraft have repeatedly tested this boundary, entering the zone on Nov. 17, Aug. 25 and June 27 of this year alone, according to Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff. Moscow has long rejected the legal basis of South Korea's identification zone and routinely fails to notify Seoul before entering, a practice that turns every approach into a guessing game that ordinary civilians pay for with their peace of mind. The South Korean Air Force scrambled F-15K fighters after detecting the Russian aircraft and conducted tactical maneuvers to prepare for contingencies. A JCS official said the planes flew close to South Korean airspace but moved away toward the East Sea after the military response. The Interior Ministry lifted the alert about three minutes later after the aircraft left the area. Yet those three minutes were enough to expose a deeper dysfunction. The English version of the initial alert read "EVACUATION, AIR RAID," a level far above the precautionary alert the military intended. SBS News reported that the ministry's message erroneously described a flight object presumed to be Russian as having violated airspace, directly contradicting the military's assessment. South Korea blames North Korea for the "invasion" Then came the second and more revealing blunder. At 7:58 a.m., North Gyeongsang Province sent its own cancellation message stating the alert was lifted "because an object presumed to be a North Korean aircraft had left the danger zone." The JoongAng Daily captured the absurdity with its headline questioning whether the aircraft were Russian or North Korean. Provincial officials later admitted they had used an outdated emergency drill template created for a North Korean aircraft scenario. It took approximately 40 minutes before the message was corrected to identify the aircraft as Russian. For the residents of Ulleung Island, who lived through real missile alerts and knew firsthand the terror of not knowing where to run, this bureaucratic theater was worse than incompetence. It was a betrayal of trust. The diplomatic response followed a script as predictable as the provocation itself. South Korea's Defense Ministry announced it would summon a Russian diplomat from the Russian Embassy in Seoul to lodge a formal protest, according to Yonhap News Agency. Yet Russia does not even recognize the legal basis of South Korea's identification zone and has stated clearly that Seoul's claimed control over it lacks foundation in international law. This diplomatic ritual of summoning an ambassador who will reject the protest's premise while the aircraft keep coming has become a meaningless dance. Under standard international practice, military aircraft entering another country's zone submit a flight plan in advance and report their position upon entry. Russia refuses to follow this protocol, and Seoul has no mechanism to compel compliance. The Russian warplanes did not fire a single shot, but they accomplished something far more insidious. They demonstrated that South Korea's defense establishment cannot distinguish a routine incursion from an invasion, cannot issue a clear warning, and cannot even correctly identify which country's aircraft is approaching its shores. When the next emergency comes, and it will, the sirens may sound again, but who will have the confidence to answer them? Sources include: Khaama.com KoreanTimes.co.kr Aljazeera.com

entries.title: US proposes up to 25% ‘excess capacity’ tariff on India, 17% if trade deal is signed | Kashmir Reader
entries.paragraph_1: NEW DELHI: The US on Wednesday proposed 25% tariffs on Indian goods in the absence of a trade deal, citing excess industrial capacity, sustained market access barriers and inadequate labour protection that harm American companies. The US Trade Representative (USTR) said the tariffs on India would amount to 17% if it agrees to a trade deal with America. The fresh tariff proposal follows Section 301 investigations launched by the USTR in March targeting 16 economic jurisdictions. The USTR proposed tariffs of up to 20% to 35% on other targeted economies, though lower rates apply to trading partners with deals in place. The EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland face 15 per cent tariff rates, inclusive of standard import duties. Vietnam would face tariffs of 20 per cent if the trade deal is finalised. “For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market-distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America’s manufacturing base,” said USTR Jamieson Greer. “India generates trade surpluses in sectors such as pharmaceuticals, steel, and ICT goods, revealing dependencies on Indian manufacturing in certain key sectors,” the USTR said in its report on ‘India’s Acts, Policies, and Practices Relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors’. These new tariffs would not be added to existing ones aimed at combating forced labour or certain sector-specific tariffs, a senior US official said. The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and sought written comments from interested persons by January 5. The Office of the USTR has been analysing for several months whether 16 jurisdictions have policies that favour surplus production, a practice that drives down prices and harms US industry. The investigation began last March, after the Supreme Court overturned the indiscriminate trade levies imposed by the Trump administration invoking the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). After that reversal, the USTR opened two investigations based on Article 301: one directed at 60 jurisdictions (about a hundred countries) for violating export regulations on forced labour; and the other against 16 jurisdictions for promoting surplus production. India and the US are negotiating an interim bilateral trade agreement after the framework they had finalised in February went back to the discussion board with the Supreme Court striking down the IEEPA tariffs imposed last year. India is seeking lower tariffs for its goods in the US market than its competitors such as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia. “USTR is applying to India a diagnosis built for a very different economy. India consumes most of what it produces and buys more goods from the world than it sells, so it is not exporting a domestic glut,” said Abhik Sengupta, a Task Force Observer on the Committee on Strategic Trade and Market Access, Helsinki Geoeconomics Society. Sengupta said India’s reliance on Chinese inputs points to gaps in its industrial base, not a surplus. “Penalising India for closing those gaps risks pushing supply chains back toward the very economies Washington is most concerned about,” he said. Trump undeterred by midterms defeat Trump reignited global trade tensions on Wednesday by proposing new tariffs on major trading powers including China, undeterred in his protectionist push by losses by his Republican Party in US midterm elections. His administration proposed levies on 14 trading partners to combat what it calls structural excess industrial capacity. The highest rate of 20% would hit China, which Washington blames for flooding world markets with cheap exports of everything from steel to electric vehicles and solar products. “We know that they don’t like these actions, but we are seeking stability with the Chinese. China is seeking stability with us,” a senior US official said, adding Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping last week was “really great”. Beijing earlier reiterated its opposition to “trade wars” and dismissed the notion of overcapacity, but stopped short of threatening retaliation. “The so-called ‘overcapacity’ is a false issue, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said, urging the world’s two top economies to maintain stable relations. The senior US official said the administration also proposed tariffs on Bangladesh, Cambodia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam. For now, Mexico and Norway are excluded from new levies. The new duties will take into account any trade deals agreed with the Trump administration and will not stack on top of some previous tariff rounds, suggesting many countries may not see a massive increase in the trading cost with the US. Even so, the prospect of new trade burdens weighed on stock markets on Wednesday as a tech-led rally continued to run out of steam. MSCI’s gauge of stocks around the globe fell 0.5%. “It is another reminder that while the legal justification for tariffs keeps changing, US protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind,” ING analysts wrote. New duties won’t exceed negotiated limits Trump’s tariffs have contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November’s midterm losses for his Republicans showed 62% of respondents would support efforts to repeal them. But Trump has long served notice of a plan to rebuild the duties the US Supreme Court struck down in February. The latest ones come after an eight-month Section 301 unfair trade practices probe. The US official also said the new duties would not exceed tariff limits in any trade deals with the Trump administration, including a 20% cap for China during Trump’s second term under a year-old truce with Beijing that is due to expire on January 10. The tariffs would also not apply to about $30 billion worth of Chinese imports that the US is considering for tariff reductions under a bilateral process, the official said. However, they would add to the tariffs on China put in place during Trump’s first term, which amounted to roughly 25%. The proposed duties will further not stack on top of tariffs of 10% or 12.5% that the administration imposed in July on a wider group of 60 trading partners over allegations of lax enforcement of anti-forced-labor laws. Specific rates are to be published in a US Federal Register notice on Wednesday. Tariff rates also will be consistent with trade agreements signed by other partners, the official said, including the 15% cap agreed by the EU, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, as well as a 19% cap agreed by Malaysia. The proposed duties will be subject to a public notice and comment period, with a hearing scheduled before they go into effect. The official said that could push implementation into January. PTI/Reuters

entries.paragraph_1: નવી દિલ્હી : આંતરરાષ્ટ્રીય સ્તરે તણાવભરી પરિસ્થિતિ વચ્ચે સાઉથ કોરિયા માં એક એવી સનસનાટીભરી ઘટના બની છે , જેણે ક્ષણભરમાં યુદ્ધ જેવો માહોલ સર્જી દીધો હતો . રશિયાના વિમાનો દેખાતા સાઉથ કોરિયાએ તાત્કાલિક પોતાના ફાઈટર જેટ્સ આકાશમાં ઉડાવ્યા હતા અને સાવચેતીના ભાગરૂપે ટાપુ ખાલી કરવાનું એલર્ટ જારી કર્યું હતું , પરંતુ માત્ર ૩ મિનિટ બાદ આ એલર્ટ પાછું ખેંચી લેવામાં આવતા ભારે હડકંપ અને ચકચાર મચી ગઈ છે . એર ડિફેન્સ આઇડેન્ટિફિકેશન ઝોન એ કોઈપણ દેશ દ્વારા પોતાની હવાઈ સીમાની સુરક્ષા માટે નક્કી કરવામાં આવેલો એક ખાસ વિસ્તાર છે . આ ઝોનની મદદથી દેશની હવાઈ સીમા તરફ આવી રહેલા કોઈપણ અજાણ્યા કે વિદેશી વિમાનની સમયસર ઓળખ કરી શકાય છે અને જરૂર પડ્યે તાત્કાલિક જવાબી કાર્યવાહી કરી શકાય છે . આ ઘટના પહેલા સાઉથ કોરિયાના સુરક્ષા મંત્રાલયે પૂર્વ કિનારે આવેલા ઉલેઉંગ ટાપુ (Ulleung island) માટે ખાલી કરવાની ચેતવણી ( ઇવેક્યુએશન વોર્નિંગ ) જાહેર કરી હતી . મંત્રાલયે તે સમયે કહ્યું હતું કે એક રશિયન વિમાન દેશની હવાઈ સીમામાં પ્રવેશ્યું છે . જોકે , માત્ર ત્રણ મિનિટ બાદ આ ચેતવણી પાછી ખેંચી લેવામાં આવી હતી . સ્થાનિક ન્યૂઝ એજન્સી ' યોનહાપ ' ના અહેવાલ મુજબ , સ્થાનિક પ્રશાસન દ્વારા ભૂલથી ઉલેઉંગ વિસ્તાર નજીક ઉત્તર કોરિયાનું વિમાન હોવાની ચેતવણી પણ થોડીવાર માટે જાહેર થઈ ગઈ હતી , જેને બાદમાં રદ કરવામાં આવી હતી .

entries.title: Russia sends 3 messages at once with strategic bomber flight near South Korea
entries.paragraph_1: Russian supersonic strategic bombers came within seconds of entering South Korean airspace near Ulleung Island on Tuesday in an unprecedented move that is raising questions about Moscow’s intentions. Russian military aircraft enter Korea’s air defense identification zone (KADIZ) several dozen times a year, but never before has a nuclear-capable strategic bomber come so close to Korean airspace. Some analysts believe Russia was seeking to demonstrate its commitment to its alliance with North Korea. According to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff, a Russian strategic bomber formation entered the KADIZ around 7:40 am on Tuesday and flew south toward Ulleung Island. By 7:52 am, the aircraft had approached within 13 nautical miles of the island and just 1 nautical mile from the boundary of Korean airspace. Another two or three seconds of flight would have taken them into Korean airspace. The South Korean military responded by scrambling several F-15K fighter jets. Russia’s Defense Ministry identified the aircraft flying over the East Sea that day as Tu-160 strategic bombers conducting a scheduled flight over international waters, according to Russia’s TASS news agency. The flight lasted approximately 10 hours, with the bombers escorted by Su-35S and Su-30SM fighter jets from the Russian Aerospace Forces. The Russian Defense Ministry said its aircraft strictly comply with international rules on the use of airspace in all flights. The Tu-160 is a supersonic long-range strategic bomber capable of carrying nuclear missiles, with a maximum range of over 12,000 kilometers. Its all-white paint scheme has earned it the moniker “White Swan.” The formation that entered KADIZ consisted of four aircraft: two Tu-160 bombers with an escort of one Su-35S and one Su-30SM fighter. Korea’s Defense Ministry summoned the Russian defense attaché, a colonel in the air force, to lodge a protest. The Foreign Ministry did not summon the Russian ambassador but expressed regret through diplomatic channels and urged Moscow to ensure that such an incident is not repeated. Russia’s Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, announced that Korean Ambassador to Russia Lee Sok-bae had met with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko to discuss pressing issues.
entries.paragraph_2: The incident was unusual in several respects. For one thing, the nuclear-capable Tu-160 strategic bomber has never before made an appearance over the East Sea (also called the Sea of Japan). Known as the world’s largest supersonic strategic bomber, the Tu-160 can carry air-launched cruise missiles fitted with nuclear warheads and reach speeds of around Mach 2. Russia gave North Korean leader Kim Jong-un a tour of its strategic bombers, including the Tu-160, during his visit to Vladivostok in September 2023. Russia has sent Tu-95MS bombers into the KADIZ on multiple previous occasions. But on this occasion, it sent the supersonic Tu-160 to the very edge of South Korean airspace, cranking up the pressure on Seoul. Russian military aircraft have recently passed through the KADIZ on their way to Japan’s air defense identification zone. This time, however, the Russian aircraft did not continue toward Japan after narrowly skirting South Korean airspace over Ulleung Island, suggesting that the operation was aimed specifically at South Korea. Experts believe Russia’s primary objective was to demonstrate to North Korea that it is fulfilling its obligations under their Treaty on Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, while also using the show of force to put pressure on the South Korean government. Russia and North Korea’s treaty, signed in June 2024, pledges mutual military assistance. Russian President Vladimir Putin emphasized the two countries’ brotherhood in arms and their commitment to the treaty in a meeting with Jo Yong-won, a senior official in North Korea’s ruling party, on Nov. 16. “The fact that Russia’s strategic bombers only brushed by South Korea this time without continuing on to Japan suggests that the operation was intended to send a message to both South and North Korea,” said Doo Jin-ho, a visiting research fellow at Kyungnam University’s Institute for Far Eastern Studies. “North Korea has sent combat troops to Russia, but Russia hadn’t previously rotated strategic assets into the region. It apparently wanted to show the North that it’s honoring its defense commitments,” Doo said. Lee Byong-chul, a professor at the same institute, said that Russia was “visibly demonstrating its commitment to defending North Korea under their bilateral treaty while also providing deterrence against the South Korea-US alliance and signaling that it could intervene in a contingency on the Korean Peninsula.” “Just as the US deploys strategic weapons to the Korean Peninsula under its mutual defense treaty with South Korea, Russia may continue deploying strategic weapons in the future as North Korea’s military backer,” Lee said.

entries.title: Kim Jong-un hints at sending tactical nukes to border with South Korea
entries.paragraph_1: After ignoring an offer of dialogue with US President Donald Trump, North Korean leader Kim Jong-un flaunted an array of nuclear warheads and facilities on Thursday, reaffirming that the North will never relinquish its nuclear weapons. Kim also threatened South Korea with a range of tactical nuclear weapons that the North is developing. North Korea’s state-run Korean Central News Agency reported on Thursday that Kim had toured “the weapons-grade nuclear materials production base, the nuclear-powered equipment production base and the nuclear weapons institute” on the previous day. The KCNA said that Kim also reviewed work at another factory that is being expanded. “This marks Kim’s fourth public visit to a facility producing nuclear materials and his first visit to the ‘nuclear-powered equipment production base,’” said an official with South Korea’s Ministry of Unification. Kim emphasized the need to develop a variety of tactical nuclear weapons that could be used to target South Korea. Kim said that North Korea “should pay attention to utilizing the tactical nukes [. . .] in multiple domains,” describing this as “an important and urgent task” arising from “tactical nukes’ military value in modern warfare and from the inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state.” Kim’s reference to sharing a border with the “most dangerous enemy state” suggests that North Korea could integrate tactical nuclear weapons into weapons systems along its border with South Korea. “The military takes very seriously North Korea’s stated intention to expand the use of tactical nuclear weapons on the Korean Peninsula,” South Korea’s Ministry of National Defense said. Another notable development is the diversification of North Korea’s nuclear warheads. In addition to the previously unveiled Hwasan-31 tactical nuclear warhead, photographs released by North Korea on Thursday showed what appeared to be a variety of Hwasan-series nuclear warheads in silver, black and red. The warhead racks bore designations including Hwasan-31-1, Hwasan-31-3, Hwasan-25, Hwasan-21, Hwasan-24, Hwasan-22 and Hwasan-14. Experts suggested that the silver hourglass-shaped warhead, being larger than the others, could be a high-yield warhead or even a hydrogen bomb. “North Korea appears to have developed a wide range of variants for the Hwasan-31 nuclear warhead that it unveiled in 2023,” said Hong Min, a senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification. “What this means is that North Korea can launch tactical nuclear weapons from a variety of air-, sea- and land-based platforms at targets anywhere on the Korean Peninsula.”
entries.paragraph_2: North Korea did not disclose the specific names or locations of the facilities Kim visited. But the International Atomic Energy Agency recently announced that North Korea had added a new facility at Yongbyon, which experts suggest may have been the site that Kim visited. Kim also took aim at South Korea’s plans to develop nuclear-powered submarines. “The US has incited its vassal states in the vicinity of our country to the possession of nuclear-powered submarines by introducing the dangerous precedent of nuclear proliferation through AUKUS to Northeast Asia,” Kim said, adding that the US is attempting to “share and use nukes with its allies.” AUKUS refers to a security partnership between Australia, the UK and the US.

entries.title: North Korean fishing boat repatriated, with crewman opting to stay in South Korea | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com
entries.paragraph_1: (Image Credit: Yonhap)
entries.paragraph_2: Seoul, November 27 (IANS) South Korea sent a North Korean fishing boat back across the sea border on Friday with six of its seven crew members aboard as one decided to stay, the unification ministry said. The vessel, found near Ulleung Island in the East Sea earlier this month, crossed the Northern Limit Line (NLL), the de facto maritime border, at 8:33 am and met two North Korean ships waiting on the other side at 9 am, the ministry said. The boat was found adrift November 3 in international waters north of the South Korean island, Yonhap News Agency reported. Of the seven North Korean men aboard, one expressed a wish to stay in the South. An official at the ministry said the man had made it clear from the outset that he did not want to go back to the North. The ministry decided to repatriate the six crewmen on humanitarian grounds. The remaining one will be protected in South Korea as a defector under relevant laws. Seoul contacted the North through the United Nations (UN) Command since the two sides have no working communication channel. The government also broadcast updates on its repatriation over the international maritime communications network from early Friday. The fact that North Korean vessels were waiting on the other side of the maritime border suggested that Pyongyang was aware of Seoul's plan to repatriate the fishing boat. Pyongyang's reaction remained unknown. Such vessels are generally repatriated by letting them sail back from the waters where they were rescued. North Korean boats and crews rescued in the East Sea in March and the Yellow Sea in May, however, were all returned in the East Sea in July. Meanwhile, a North Korean defector has been taken into police custody after entering a civilian restricted area near the inter-Korean border and is currently undergoing questioning, a military official said on Friday. The military found the woman in her 30s at around 6:40 pm on Thursday between a village north of the Civilian Control Line (CCL) and the general outpost fence in the border county of Cheorwon, about 75 kilometers northeast of Seoul, a Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) official said. Police and relevant authorities are questioning her over possible espionage linked to North Korea, among other suspicions, the JCS official said. The woman had crossed the CCL, which runs just south of the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) separating the two Koreas, and was heading north toward the heavily fortified GOP area secured with barbed-wire fences, according to military officials. She had come as close as about 200 meters to the GOP line before being apprehended. While public access to the CCL area is restricted, several civilian villages remain inside the zone, with residents commuting to and from their homes using special permits. The woman was found to have reached a village of about 500 residents inside the CCL, where local authorities operate shuttle buses for residents. "The investigation is under way to find out how the woman reached the village," a JCS official added.

entries.paragraph_1: 한미약품 최인영 부사장 ‘국민훈장 목련장’ 수훈
entries.paragraph_2: 지난 25일 서울 서초구 JW 메리어트 호텔에서 열린 ‘2026 보건산업 성과교류회’에서 한미약품 미래성장부문장 최인영 부사장(왼쪽 세번째)이 임직원들과 함께 기념촬영을 하고 있다. 한미그룹 제공 한미약품 미래성장부문장 최인영 부사장이 ‘국민훈장 목련장’을 수훈했다. 27일 한미약품에 따르면 국민훈장 목련장은 정치·경제·사회·교육·학술 분야에서 국민 복지 향상과 국가 발전에 기여한 공적이 뚜렷한 인물에게 수여하는 훈장이다. 최 부사장은 지난 25일 ‘2026 보건산업 성과교류회’ 보건의료기술진흥 유공자 정부포상 시상식에서 국민훈장 목련장을 받았다. 최 부사장은 혁신신약 개발과 글로벌 기술수출을 주도하고, 국내 개발 항암 분야 바이오신약 최초의 미국 식품의약국(FDA) 허가와 상용화를 이끄는 등 한국 보건의료기술 발전과 제약바이오 산업의 글로벌 경쟁력 강화에 기여한 공로를 인정받았다. 1998년 한미약품 연구원으로 입사한 최 부사장은 비만·대사질환과 희귀질환, 항암 등 다양한 분야에서 혁신신약 개발을 주도해 왔다. 연구개발(R&D) 성과를 글로벌 기술수출과 신약 상용화로 연결하며 한미약품의 경쟁력 강화에도 기여해 왔다. 최 부사장은 스펙트럼, 머크 등 글로벌 제약사와의 기술수출을 이끌어 왔으며 올해에는 일라이 릴리와 단장증후군 치료제 ‘소네페글루타이드’의 기술수출 과정에서도 주요 역할을 맡았다. 신약 상용화 과정에서도 성과를 냈다. 최 부사장은 호중구감소증 치료 바이오신약 ‘롤론티스’ 개발에 기여해 2022년 국내 항암 분야 바이오신약 최초로 미국 식품의약국(FDA) 허가와 상용화를 이끌었다. 롤론티스는 기술 혁신성과 사업화 성과를 인정받아 올해 국내 최고 권위의 산업기술상인 ‘IR52 장영실상’을 수상했다. 최 부사장은 “이번 국민훈장 목련장은 한미의 모든 연구원들이 오랜 기간 함께 축적해 온 연구개발 역량과 혁신을 향한 도전의 결과”라며 “혁신신약을 지속 창출해 대한민국 보건의료기술 발전과 제약바이오 산업의 글로벌 경쟁력 강화에 기여할 것”이라고 말했다.
